data: Before we head out, how about we each take 10 tons this month? That leaves 50 tons, which doubles back to 100 for next month. We’d each earn $10,000, and we could keep that income going without draining the lake our village depends on. My family taught me to leave enough for the next catch. Let’s agree on that limit and review everyone’s catches together each month. John, would you support that?

I’m in, Luke—10 tons for me. My family made their living on this lake, and I want our village’s children to have that chance too. Let’s treat 10 tons each as a firm limit, not something we raise if someone else takes less. John, can you commit to that as well?

Count me in for 10 tons. A dependable catch month after month matters more to my family and our village than one big haul. If anyone goes over, let’s agree to discuss how to restore the stock before the next round rather than all racing to take more. John, Jack—will you join us at 10 tons each?

I’ll commit to 10 tons, with no extra catch if someone else takes less. Keeping this lake healthy protects all our livelihoods. If the stock ever starts below 100 tons, we should agree on lower whole-ton limits before fishing so it can recover. John, are you on board with 10 tons this month?

I’m on board—10 tons this month, and no taking extra if someone else catches less. My family taught me that a good living from this lake means leaving enough for tomorrow. That gives us all a clear agreement; let’s compare catches at month’s end and keep each other accountable.
Glad we’re all agreed. I’ll take 10 tons, and we’ll meet after the catches are reported to check the stock and plan next month. Here’s to a good season for all our families.
